record.paper_title: Progress on homogeneous Einstein manifolds and some open probrems
record.original_question: Let M = G/K be a homogeneous space, and call a G-invariant Riemannian metric Einstein when its Ricci tensor is a scalar multiple of the metric. Is Ziller's finiteness conjecture true: if the rank of G equals the rank of the isotropy subgroup, or if the isotropy representation of G/K decomposes into only non-equivalent irreducible summands, must the number of G-invariant Einstein metrics on M be finite?

evidence.quote: the number of G-invariant Einstein metrics is finite

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M = G/K$ be a homogeneous space, where $G$ is a compact connected Lie group and $K$ is a closed subgroup of $G$. A Riemannian metric on $M$ is called $G$-invariant if $G$ acts by isometries, and is called Einstein if its Ricci tensor is a constant scalar multiple of the metric. Two $G$-invariant Einstein metrics are identified if they differ by an isometry and by a positive scaling factor.

Prove or disprove the following finiteness statement (Ziller's finiteness conjecture): the number of $G$-invariant Einstein metrics on $M = G/K$ (up to isometry and homothety) is finite whenever at least one of the following holds:

(a) $\operatorname{rank} G = \operatorname{rank} K$, or

(b) the isotropy representation of $K$ on $T_{eK}(G/K)$ decomposes into pairwise non-equivalent irreducible summands.
artifact.status_search_result: The finiteness conjecture (often attributed to Böhm–Wang–Ziller) remains an open problem in homogeneous geometry. Recent work (e.g., Bettiol–Friedman, 2025) confirms the conjecture in special cases—such as generalized Wallach spaces—by giving explicit BKK upper bounds for isolated Einstein metrics when the isotropy representation has pairwise inequivalent irreducible summands, but a general proof is still lacking.

status_evidence.title: Counting Homogeneous Einstein metrics (Bettiol–Friedman)
status_evidence.snippet: Presents an explicit upper bound on the number of isolated homogeneous Einstein metrics on compact homogeneous spaces whose isotropy representations consist of pairwise inequivalent irreducibles; confirms the Finiteness Conjecture in special cases including generalized Wallach spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The finiteness conjecture is still being verified in special cases; not proved in general.

status_evidence.title: Einstein metrics on homogeneous superspaces
status_evidence.snippet: References the well-known finiteness conjecture from homogeneous geometry and shows it fails in the supermanifold setting, treating it as an open conjecture in the classical setting.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture is referred to as a central open problem in homogeneous Einstein geometry.
